scenes.headline: How Open 3D Skills explodes a machine and films it
scenes.sub: A staging rule, and a clock the page cannot see past.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pinion! Open 3D Skills is eight agent skills for 3D web pages. Here's how two of them work.

scenes.text: A skill is a procedure, not a model: one takes a machine apart in stages, another films any page at 60 fps by owning its clock.
scenes.say: A skill is a procedure, not a model. One takes a machine apart in stages. Another films any page by owning its clock.

items.say: Make every part one group, with its own materials.
Give each part a stage. Shells leave first, the way a mechanic works.
Give it an offset, or let it move away from the centre.
Labels sit in two columns, never over the model.

parts.say: With n stages, each one gets a window of two over n plus one.

parts.note: starts when the last is half done
parts.say: Each stage starts when the one before is half done, so the last ends exactly at one.

steps.say: Before the page loads, the recorder replaces its clock, and moves time forward one sixtieth of a second per frame.
It runs the page's frame callbacks once, however long they take.
It takes a screenshot and pipes it to ffmpeg.
Then it loops. The page never sees that each frame took a tenth of a second.

scenes.label: frame rate of the file, from a page drawing 12 frames a second
scenes.note: 360 frames in 6 s, measured on CPU
scenes.say: The page drew about twelve frames a second. The file came out at exactly sixty.

scenes.title: Two ways to film a page

left.title: Page draws frame i
items: The page is written to be recorded
Frames read straight off the canvas
left.say: This site's own film engines ask the page to draw any frame on request.

right.title: Recorder owns the clock
items: Works on pages not written for it
Timers and new Date keep real time
right.say: Frame capture takes the clock away instead. It works on any page, but timers still read real time.

scenes.text: Read time from performance.now and the frame timestamp, and a slow page still films at a perfect 60 fps.
scenes.say: Read time from the page clock, not timers, and a slow page still films at sixty frames a second.

recap: Parts leave in stages, shells first
A virtual clock steps one sixtieth per frame
Move timers onto the page clock
scenes.say: To recap: parts leave in stages, a virtual clock steps one frame at a time, and timers belong on the page clock.
